title: Vegan Cilantro Radish Chimichurri
description: This vegan cilantro radish chimichurri comes together in 15 minutes with no cooking required. Fresh cilantro and homegrown radish give it a peppery, herby kick ...

items: 1 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
1/2 shallot, chopped
2 tbsp dried parsley
1 tbsp dried oregano
1/2 cup olive oil
1/4 cup white wine vinegar
1 tbsp lemon juice
1 tbsp red pepper flakes (gochugaru or regular), to taste
1 tbsp radish, finely chopped
1 tsp garlic, finely chopped
1 tsp sea salt, to taste
Black pepper, to taste

steps.name: Chop the Cilantro and Radish
items: Wash and finely chop the fresh cilantro.
Wash and finely chop the radish into small, crisp rounds.
Dice 1/2 a shallot.

steps.name: Stir Together the Chimichurri
items: Combine all ingredients in a small bowl and stir with a fork, ideally using a bowl with a lid for easy fridge storage.
Taste and adjust: add more vinegar for brightness, more red pepper flakes for heat, or more salt to balance.

steps.name: Spoon Over Vegan Steak and Serve
items: Generously spoon the chimichurri over vegan steak and serve immediately for the freshest flavor.

tips: Fresh cilantro works best; it's fine to use some dried herbs, but ideally keep the amount of dried herbs below the amount of fresh.
The radish is optional, but it adds a nice extra dimension of flavor, crunch, and color if you have it on hand.
This chimichurri isn't just for vegan steak: try it on vegan tacos, toasted focaccia, or any dish with vegan protein. It brightens things up with a ton of freshness and kick.

title: No-Bake Vegan Peanut Butter Chocolate Cheesecake Cups
description: These no-bake vegan peanut butter chocolate cheesecake cups are creamy, rich, and completely dairy-free. Made with a date and almond flour crust, a silky cashew...

items: 1 1/4 cups almond flour
5-6 medjool dates, pitted
2 heaping tablespoons peanut butter
1/2 teaspoon salt (for the crust)
1 cup salted cashews
1/2 cup full-fat coconut milk
1/3 cup maple syrup
1/4 cup coconut oil, melted
1 tablespoon lemon juice
1/2 teaspoon salt (for the filling)
1 cup vegan chocolate chips

steps.name: Make the Crust
items: Add the almond flour, dates, peanut butter, and 1/2 tsp of salt to a food processor. Blend until thoroughly combined.
Line a muffin pan with liners and press a thin, even layer of crust into the bottom of each one.

steps.name: Blend and Pour the Filling
items: In the same food processor, add the cashews, coconut milk, maple syrup, coconut oil, lemon juice, and 1/2 tsp of salt. Blend until completely smooth.
Pour the filling in each muffin cup so each one is just about full.
Place the muffin pan in the freezer for 1 hour to chill.

steps.name: Add the Chocolate Topping
items: Melt the chocolate chips in a small microwave-safe bowl in 30-second intervals, stirring between each, until smooth.
Spoon a small amount of melted chocolate over the top of each cup.
Put the muffin cups back into to the freezer to chill for 10 minutes, then serve.

tips: Use the thick, fatty part of the coconut milk for the creamiest filling.

title: Easy Vegan Fried Rice (Great for Leftover Rice)
description: This easy vegan fried rice is the perfect way to use up leftover rice and turn it into a satisfying meal in under 30 minutes. Made with crispy vegan chicken str...

items: 1 red onion (or white onion)
1 tbsp chopped garlic
1 red bell pepper
2-4 tbsp soy sauce
12-16 oz bag of vegan chicken strips (or 1 block of tofu, cubed)
2-3C cooked white rice (dried leftover rice is ideal)
1-2 tbsp avocado oil (or any high heat point oil)
2-4 tbsp vegan butter
1 tsp sesame oil (optional)
ground black pepper (to taste)

steps.name: Stir-Fry the Vegetables
items: Chop the red onion into small pieces.
Heat the avocado oil in a pan until it ripples, then add the onion and fry.
While the onion cooks, chop the red bell pepper into small squares.
Once the onions separate and turn translucent, add the red bell pepper and stir-fry together.

steps.name: Air-Fry the Protein
items: Air fry the frozen vegan chicken strips until chewy and crispy, 10–20 minutes at 400°F.
Just before removing the protein from the air fryer, add the chopped garlic and stir, cooking for another minute.
Add the cooked protein to the veggie stir-fry and stir to combine.
Add 2–4 tbsp vegan butter and stir until melted.

steps.name: Add the Rice and Season
items: Add the cooked white rice to the pan with the buttery stir-fried veggies and protein.
Add 2–4 tbsp soy sauce to taste and stir to combine.
Once the rice has absorbed the liquid and is heated through, it's ready to serve. Remove from heat promptly to avoid mushiness.
Season with a splash of 1 tsp sesame oil and ground black pepper to taste.

tips: Don't cook the rice too long after adding it since once it's hydrated and heated through, serve immediately to avoid mushiness.
For the protein, you can use cubed tofu instead of vegan chicken strips and air fry at 400°F for 20 min until crispy.
Swap avocado oil for any high-heat oil (vegetable, refined coconut, etc.).
You can use white or red onion since both work great.

title: Crispy Sourdough Discard Crackers (Easy, Vegan, 4 Ingredients)
description: Turn leftover sourdough discard into crispy, golden herb crackers with just a few pantry staples. An easy, budget-friendly zero-waste snack.

items: 300g sourdough discard
4 tbsp (56g) vegan butter (melted)
4 tsp mixed dried herbs
1/2 tsp (2g) salt for sprinkling on top
Preheat the oven to 350F (176C).
Melt the vegan butter in a small cup in the microwave and let cool.
Weigh the sourdough discard, dried herbs into a medium-sized mixing bowl.
Add melted butter to the mixing bowl and stir thoroughly until well-combined.
Use a spatula to spread the mixture into a thin, even layer onto a baking sheet with parchment paper, or just put it directly onto a truly nonstick baking sheet.
Sprinkle salt on top of the mixture.
Bake for 10 minutes.
Remove from oven and score the crackers. (optional)
Bake for an additional 25 min until crackers are golden brown.
Break the crispy pieces off the edges, and put the tray back into the oven to finish cooking the crackers with the residual heat.

tips: Between loaves of sourdough bread is the best time to make these because it uses up pretty much the exact amount of starter you want to use up and it makes room for you to feed your starter again.
Don’t worry about having to use active sourdough discard (can be active or non-active), as both work well!
If you want, you can score the crackers at 10 min in the oven, but it’s not necessary, it just helps with presentation.

title: Gourmet Vegan Oat Milk Hot Chocolate (Rich, Creamy, Maple-Sweetened)
description: This gourmet oat milk hot chocolate is naturally dairy-free and ready in just 10 minutes. Made from scratch with cocoa powder, coconut milk, and maple syrup, it...

items: 1/4 C cocoa powder
1 ½ C oat milk
½ C full-fat coconut milk
2-4 tbsp of maple syrup
Dash of salt
2 cinnamon sticks (or cinnamon powder) (optional)
Dash of ground cardamom (optional)
In a medium pot, add cocoa powder, oat milk, coconut milk, and a dash of salt.
If you’d like a more dark chocolate flavored and less sweet hot chocolate, then add 2 tbsp of maple syrup. If you prefer more sweet, then add 3-4 tbsp of maple syrup.
Turn the heat on medium and whisk to combine.
Let it reduce a bit by simmering for ~5 min.
Pour into mugs, add a cinnamon stick, and top with a dash of cardamom powder!

tips: For the creamiest results, I don’t recommend swapping out the full-fat coconut milk, since you need something dense to achieve a silky texture.
Whisk the cocoa and liquid ingredients over medium heat to prevent lumps and ensure smoothness.

title: Air Fryer Biscoff Baklava “Egg” Rolls (Vegan & Date-Sweetened)
description: Crispy air fryer Biscoff baklava “egg” rolls filled with sweet dates, cashews, warm cinnamon, and a hint of maple syrup, finished with a light lemon maple glaze...

items: 6 plant-based “egg” roll wrappers (Nasoya)
6 Medjool dates (pitted)
⅔ cup raw cashews
2 tbsp cookie butter spread (Lotus Biscoff)
1 tbsp maple syrup (for the filling)
Pinch of salt
½ tsp ground cinnamon
1 tbsp water (for the glaze)
1 tsp lemon juice (for the glaze)
1/4 C maple syrup (for the glaze)

steps.name: Make the filling
items: Add the dates, cashews, Biscoff spread, 1 tbsp maple syrup, salt, and cinnamon to a food processor.
Blend until mostly smooth but still slightly textured like traditional baklava filling. Scrape down sides as needed.

steps.name: Roll the “egg” rolls
items: Lay one “egg” roll wrapper flat in a diamond shape.
Add 2–3 tablespoons of filling near the center.
Fold the bottom corner over the filling, fold in the sides, and roll tightly upward.
Lightly seal the edge with water.
Repeat with remaining wrappers. It’s okay and preferable if you have some of the crumb left, since you can top the “egg” rolls with it!

steps.name: Air fry
items: No need to preheat, just throw in the 6 “egg” rolls into the air fryer basket and start cooking them on 400F.
Cook on 400F for 3 minutes and 30 seconds, then flip the plant-based “egg” rolls to ensure even crispiness.
Cook for 2 more minutes and then flip again.
Continue cooking flipping each minute or so (~8 minutes total) until golden and crisp.

steps.name: Make the glaze
items: In a small saucepan, combine maple syrup, lemon juice, and water.
Bring to a gentle simmer for 2–3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Remove from heat.

steps.name: Finish and serve
items: Drizzle warm lemon maple glaze over the crispy “egg” rolls.
Sprinkle on some of the reserved crumb from the filling.
Let sit for a minute or two so the glaze lightly soaks in.
Serve warm for best texture.
Serving suggestion: These “egg” rolls are rich and indulgent, so one, maybe two, is plenty per person.

tips: Don’t overfill the wrappers or they may burst while air frying.
Flip twice during cooking to ensure even crispiness.
These are best enjoyed fresh but can be reheated in the air fryer for 2–3 minutes to re-crisp.
Best if eaten within 2 days.

title: Crispy Vegan Salt and Pepper Air Fryer Tofu with Stir-Fried Veggies
description: Crispy vegan salt and pepper tofu made in the air fryer with Chinese five spice, paprika, and stir-fried veggies in a savory balsamic soy sauce.

items: 1 firm tofu
1 tsp ground white pepper (for tofu rub)
1/2 tsp salt (for tofu rub)
1/2 tsp Chinese five spice powder (for tofu rub)
1/4 tsp paprika (for tofu rub)
3-4 tbsp cornstarch (for tofu crispiness)
2 tbsp balsamic vinegar (for stir fry)
1 tbsp rice wine vinegar (for stir fry)
4 tbsp soy sauce (for stir fry)
1 tsp Sichuan chili oil (optional - to taste for stir fry)
1 tsp sesame oil (for stir fry)
2 tbsp coconut oil
1/2 large white onion
1 bell pepper
3 large portobello mushrooms
2 cloves garlic
1 stalk of scallion
1 cup white rice (optional)

steps.name: Prep the tofu and rice
items: Prepare the firm tofu by pressing it for ~15 minutes or so.
Preheat your air fryer to 375F. We will use this temperature to cook the tofu!

While the tofu is being pressed and the air fryer is pre-heating, heat up a small pot of boiling water and start making a side of white rice (omit this step if you are good with tofu and veggies only). Otherwise, move on to chopping up veggies for the stir fry.

steps.name: Prep the stir fry ingredients
items: Chop up half a large white onion, bell pepper, and portobello into small pieces.
Finely chop up 2 garlic gloves and 1 green onion.

steps.name: Make tofu seasoning and coat the tofu
items: Create the tofu rub by combining the ground white pepper, salt, Chinese five spice powder, paprika together ideally in a shallow wide bowl so it’ll be easier to roll the tofu cubes in it.

After pressing the tofu, cut up the tofu into small 1” cubes and roll them into the wide plate of spices. No need to press the spices in too hard, since we don’t want it to taste too dry from excess spices on each tofu.

Next, evenly coat the tofu with cornstarch by working in small batches to keep the cornstarch dry. If your wide spice plate is dry, add the cornstarch to it and roll the tofu cubes until coated on all sides. If the plate is wet from previous tofu, rinse and dry it before adding fresh cornstarch.

steps.name: Air Fry the Tofu
items: Add the cornstarch and spice covered tofu into the air fryer and cook for 15 min, turning the tofu halfway through.

steps.name: Stir Fry the Vegetables
items: While the tofu is air frying heat up a large skillet on high and add a tablespoon of coconut oil (or ideally some high smoke point oil).
Once heated, add the chopped onion and cook for a few minutes until they start to show a hint of color at the edges.
Add the chopped bell pepper, stir, and cook again for a few minutes. Reduce the heat to medium if the onion starts to crisp up too much.
Add the chopped mushrooms, finely chopped garlic, and the chopped green onion and stir, cooking for another 2 minutes or so.

Add the balsamic vinegar, rice vinegar, soy sauce, Sichuan chili oil to the veggie stir fry. Cook for 2-4 minutes to lessen the flavor potency of the vinegars, and let the sauce reduce a bit more and infuse with the veggies.
Once the sauce mostly evaporated, and you tasted a small pepper piece for “doneness”, if the pepper is cooked to your liking, you can add a tsp of sesame oil for more flavor at the very end.

steps.name: Finish and serve
items: Add a tbsp of coconut oil to the skillet again and toss in the air fried tofu cubes and mix for another minute or so the sauce caramelizes a bit, then remove from heat.
Add cooked rice to a deeper set plate or small bowl and top it with the stir fry veggie tofu mix and enjoy!

tips: Only coat a few tofu cubes with cornstarch at a time so the cornstarch doesn’t get wet and clump.
Frozen pre-chopped veggies or frozen stir fry veggies can be used to save time!

title: Vegan Cinnamon Sugar Air Fryer Donut Holes (Ready in 20 Minutes)
description: These vegan cinnamon sugar air fryer donut holes are a quick and easy breakfast or dessert made with simple pantry ingredients and no yeast or deep frying. Soft...

items: 200 g all-purpose flour
50 g granulated sugar
120 g vegan vanilla yogurt (Forager is ideal)
25 g plant-based milk
1 tsp baking powder
1 tsp vanilla extract
2 tbsp melted coconut oil
50 g granulated sugar (for topping)
1 tbsp ground cinnamon (for topping)
1 tbsp melted coconut oil (for topping)
Preheat the air fryer to 350F.
Combine all but topping ingredients into a large mixing bowl.
Mix it with a stand mixer (or it can also be mixed by hand to cut down on cleaning effort).
Form ten balls (~1” in diameter). In my first batch, I tried 8, but it needed a longer cook time.
Add the 10 donut holes into the air fryer and cook for 5 min on each side for a total of 10 minutes.

As the donut holes are air frying, melt 1 tbsp of coconut oil in a small, round, tea cup (or something similar so it’s easier to dip the donut holes into the oil before sprinkling on the cinnamon sugar topping).
Make the cinnamon sugar mix by mixing 50 g of sugar with 1 tbsp of cinnamon.
Once the donuts finished air frying, coat each one with melted coconut oil and top with cinnamon sugar on all sides.

tips: Best enjoyed right after cooking! Store in an airtight container for at most a few days.
Smaller balls will ensure that the donuts cook evenly and all the way through!

title: Easy Vegan Tofu Scramble (High-Protein, 15-Minute Breakfast)
description: This quick vegan tofu scramble is a simple, protein-packed breakfast made with firm tofu, warming spices, and pantry staples. Ready in just 15 minutes, it has a...

items: 1 firm tofu
1-2 tbsp ground turmeric
2 tsp garlic powder
2 tsp onion powder
1-2 tsp dried parsley
1 tbsp olive oil
1/2 C vegan liquid egg (Egg from Plants, previously Just Egg) (optional)
2 tsp salt (to taste)
1 tsp ground black pepper (to taste)
nutritional yeast (to taste if you like cheesiness)
Heat up a large skillet on medium heat, then add a tbsp of olive oil.
Add the firm tofu block to the pan (unpressed), and mash it with a potato masher until it becomes more crumbly and looks similar to scrambled egg texture.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add turmeric and stir thoroughly. Adjust the amount based off how dark yellow you’d like your eggs. This is mainly for coloring!
Add the garlic powder and onion powder.
For a bit more realism and a bit more creaminess, add 1/3 to 1/2 a mini carton’s worth of “Egg from Plants” in the gaps on the pan where no tofu egg is.
Stir, and continue stirring occasionally until fully cooked through.
Add parsley and stir.

tips: This vegan egg pairs really well with my vegan breakfast tacos for dinner recipe!

title: Creamy Vegan Tzatziki Sauce (Easy Dairy-Free Greek Yogurt Recipe)
description: Yes, this tzatziki is naturally vegan. This easy, budget-friendly sauce uses vegan Greek yogurt, fresh cucumber, garlic, lemon, and dill. Creamy, tangy, and com...

items: 1/2 large english cucumber
1 pint of greek vegan yogurt (plain)
2 cloves of garlic
2 tsp salt
2 tbsp red wine vinegar
4 tbsp olive oil
dill to taste
lemon juice to taste
Add everything to the food processor except the lemon juice.
Next, blend all the ingredients together until the mixture is smooth without any chunks of veggies.
Taste it and add lemon juice and salt as needed.

tips: This vegan tzatziki pairs really well with my vegan focaccia recipe!

title: Vegan Mexican Hot Chocolate Snickerdoodles (Cinnamon Cocoa Cookies with a Spicy Kick)
description: These Vegan Mexican Hot Chocolate Snickerdoodles are a quick, budget-friendly dessert made with pantry staples and bold flavors. Inspired by traditional Mexican...

items: 1/2 C vegan butter
1 C granulated sugar (and ~1/3 C for coating the cookies)
1/4 C maple syrup
3 tbsp plant-based milk
2 tsp vanilla extract
1 2/3 C all-purpose flour
1/2 C cocoa powder
1 tsp baking soda
1/4 tsp salt
1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
1/2 tsp cayenne

steps.name: Cream the Butter and Sugar
items: In your stand mixer bowl, add 1/2 C vegan butter and 1 C of sugar and cream until light and fluffy.
Next, add the maple syrup, plant milk, vanilla extract and mix again.

steps.name: Add Dry Ingredients
items: Add the rest of the dry ingredients and stir until combined.
Chill the dough for ~5 min.
Preheat the oven to 350F.

steps.name: Shape the Cookies
items: For each batch of cookies (you will end with 3 batches), roll out into 9 walnut-sized balls and coat each with some sugar.
Flatten the balls lightly with 2 fingers so that they make ~2 in sized disks. (Space the cookies ~1 in apart as they spread a lot during cooking!)

steps.name: Bake and Cool
items: Bake for 10-12 min (I usually do 12 min) at 350F. While the batch bakes, keep the remaining dough chilled in the fridge. Repeat for the remaining 2 batches of 9 cookies each.
Remove the cookies from the oven and let them cool for ~5 min.
Transfer to a cooling rack or a plate to cool completely.

tips: If you don’t like medium spicy foods as much, then half the cayenne.
Space out the cookies enough on the baking sheet as they spread out a lot during baking.

title: Easy Vegan Chicken and Potato Air Fryer  Wraps
description: Get crispy, delicious vegan chicken and potato wraps made fast in your air fryer. This quick recipe is ready in under 30 minutes for lazy mornings!

items: Frozen vegan chicken strips
Scallion
Large flour tortillas (I prefer the spinach ones)
Vegan shredded mozzarella (violife is pretty good)
1 tbsp of olive oil
4 medium russet potatoes
Salt to taste
Ground black pepper to taste
1-2 tbsp ground cumin
1-2 tbsp paprika
Salsa
Airfry the vegan chicken for 5-7min until you notice slight crispiness on the edges.
While air frying the chicken, wash and cut the russet potatoes into small bite sized cubes.
Heat up the cast iron on high and once up to temp, turn it down to medium, then add the olive oil and cubed potatoes.
Stir the potatoes to coat them in oil, then add salt and ground pepper to taste along with around 1-2 tbsp of cumin and paprika.
Once the chicken is crispy, remove it from the air fryer and transfer it to a medium sized bowl.
Transfer the cooking cubed potatoes to finish up cooking in the air fryer.
Transfer the vegan chicken strips into the cast iron.
Throw in finely chopped green onion and stir.
Add one tbsp or chopped garlic to the pan and stir.
Cook for another 5 minutes or so or until it looks fully done.
Take out a tortilla, then add the vegan cheese, crispy chicken and onion mixture, and the air fried potatoes. Top the mix with additional cheese to ensure everything stays put.
Wrap the tortilla up on all sides, then transfer it to the air fryer to crisp up and melt the cheesy inside, around 3 min as it should already be preheated to temperature from the earlier steps.
Cut the wrap in half and serve with a generous portion of salsa!

title: Golden Brown Vegan Sourdough Focaccia (Longer Proof)
description: Stop buying overpriced bread! Make perfect vegan sourdough focaccia at home. This recipe yields a pillowy inside and crunchy crust.

items: 440g oat milk
125g sourdough starter (freshly fed)
525g bread flour
10-15g salt
Salt (to taste)
Garlic powder (optional - to taste)
Rosemary (optional - to taste)
Mix oat milk, sourdough and salt with a stand mixer if you have one or a silicone spatula.
Then add the bread flour and mix again.
Slick the surface of the dough with olive oil.
Cover the bowl with a lid/cloth and leave out at room temperature for 8 hours or until it doubles in volume.
Once proofed, transfer to a non-stick baking sheet.
Flatten it out and then add the toppings.
Preheat oven to 450F.
Bake at 450F.

tips: Experiment with smoky salt, finely chopped olives.
At different altitudes, you may need to adjust the amount of liquid you add.

title: Multi-Meal Prep Vegan Chili (Easy, High-Protein, Budget-Friendly)
description: Make hearty, delicious multi-meal prep vegan chili! This easy recipe uses ground meat substitute, kidney beans, crushed tomatoes, and bold spices.

items: 2-4 tbsp olive oil
24 oz of vegan ground beef (morning star or gardein)
1 large red onion
2 small (or 1 large) bell peppers (any color)
1 C frozen corn
1/2 C of pickle juice (or wine, vinegar, or beer)
2-3 cloves of garlic
vegetable bouillon (2 cubes)
32 oz canned kidney beans (or chili beans)
28 oz of crushed tomatoes (tutto rosso is a good brand, cheap and tasty)
4 tbsp ground cumin
1 tsp smoked paprika (or 1 tbsp of hickory liquid smoke)
1 tsp ground black pepper to taste
2-3 jalapeno peppers (optional)
Chop the red onion into 1 in pieces.
Sauté onion in 2-4 tbsp olive oil on high until clear or charred. (based on your preference)
Chop peppers into 1/2 in pieces.
Throw in chopped peppers with the onion to cook. Sauté peppers and onions together a bit in a large pot, for ~5-7 min. (Can also add optional chopped jalapano as well)
Add 1 cup of frozen corn to the pot, and continue sautéing (can raise the temperature if it lowers a lot from adding the frozen corn).
Add 2-3 cloves of garlic, finely chopped into the pot and stir.
Open the can(s) of kidney beans, rinse the beans, then add the beans to the pot and stir.
Once its been thoroughly stir fried, add 1 can of crushed tomatoes.
Add the 1/2 C of liquid (beer, pickle juice, wine, etc).
Add 4 tbsp cumin seed powder.
Once cumin is well dissolved in the chili.
Add 2 cubes of vegan bullion and stir. Lower heat to medium low (slow simmer).
Add 1 tsp smoked paprika or 1 tbsp liquid smoke (to taste).
Add pepper to taste and stir.
Add 2 12 oz bags of vegan ground beef and bring temperature up to medium. (it’s fine to add this in at the end since vegan beef cooks pretty quickly).
Cook for 30 min - 1 hr more and serve!

tips: Don’t add the 1/2 C of liquid before frying the veggies otherwise they will have more of a boiled quality rather than a sautéd quality.

title: One-Bowl Vegan Sourdough Discard Blueberry Pancakes (No Eggs, Dairy-Free)
description: Whip up the easiest breakfast with this one-bowl vegan sourdough discard pancake recipe! These fluffy, dairy-free pancakes are the perfect way to use up sourdou...

items: 290g oat milk
50g water
20g vanilla extract
100g sourdough discard
2g table salt
240g all-purpose flour
60g granulated sugar
12g baking powder
1C frozen blueberries (ideally organic as they’re more tart)
Coconut oil (for greasing the pan)
Maple syrup (for topping the pancakes)
Add oat milk, vanilla, and water to a mixing bowl first, so that when you add the sourdough discard next, it doesn’t stick to the bowl.
Add the sourdough discard to the bowl and stir.
Add the salt to the wet mixture and stir, so that it dissolves well.
Add the rest of the dry ingredients to the mixing bowl.
Mix all ingredients with a spatula.
Turn on your skillet’s heat to medium and let it get up to temperature.  Add 1 tbsp coconut oil to coat the pan.
Wait until the oil starts to look slightly wavy and shimmer. That will mean it’s up to temperature, and you’ll have a much easier time flipping the pancakes without them sticking to the pan.

Using the spatula, dollop 3 pancakes on the pan. When dolloping the pancakes onto the pan, make sure to flatten them a bit more so they aren’t too thick. That way, the pancakes will cook all the way through. I find the sourdough helps them keep their thickness, but you need to watch out that the pancakes aren’t too thick from the get-go before flipping.
Rotate the pan to ensure the coconut oil has a chance to hit the edges of all the pancakes for easy flipping.

Wait 30 seconds to 1 minute, and then once the pancakes show bubbles and their edges are firmed up, flip them with a separate flipper/clean spatula. They should be very easy to flip! If they aren’t then you may have flipped them too soon, didn’t wait until the pan got up to temperature, or used the wrong type of oil.
Between batches, I add a little bit more coconut oil to coat the pan.

If the pan is steaming a ton, you may want to lower the heat a bit below medium. The pancakes will take longer to cook, but it will be easier to understand when to flip them. (Otherwise, the pancakes might be flipped too soon or stick to the pan).
If the pan doesn’t have any steam at all, you may want to raise the temperature slightly above medium, such that when you add the pancakes it sizzles.
Continue until all pancakes are cooked (it should make around 3-4 medium sized pancakes for ~2 people for 2 mornings).

title: Quick Vegan Breakfast Tacos for Dinner (30-Minute Leftover Recipe)
description: Turn leftover taco fixings into a quick, 30-minute vegan dinner! These breakfast-style tacos are packed with flavor and use a simple red wine vinegar marinade.

items: 6-10 small corn tortillas (for 2 people)
1 tbsp chopped garlic
1-2 tbsp red wine vinegar
1 small red onion
1 tbsp vegan butter
1 tbsp adobo paste (I suggest Chef Merito Birria Marinade | Authentic Mexican Flavor)
salsa to taste
dash of chili lime seasoning (Trader Joe's, optional)
hot sauce (optional)
1/4 C vegan egg (optional leftovers from previous breakfast)
1/4 C cubed potatoes (optional leftovers from previous breakfast)

Begin by air frying the vegan meat on 400F for around 10 min while you chop up the red onion and sear it (doesn’t matter if you count preheat time with this as you’ll finish up cooking the vegan meat in a skillet).
Chop up the small red onion and fry/sear for a few minutes.
Add the vegan meat to the skillet on medium and break it apart. Don’t forget to add the airfryer oil also to the pan that dripped off the vegan meat.
Add 1 tbsp of chopped garlic and stir.
Add 1 tbsp of adobo sauce to the meat and stir.
Add 1 tbsp red wine vinegar if you’d like and stir.
Cook vegan meat to desired crispiness and in the last 2 min, add 1 tbsp of vegan butter to unstick the vegan meat from the pan (bump pan’s temperature to medium/high if you want it more charred).
You can add a dash of Trader Joe’s chili lime powder or cumin if you’d like, adjust seasoning as desired.
When the vegan beef is about done, air fry the taco shells for around 1-3 min for desired crunchiness.
Assemble, add a little salsa, and serve!

title: High-Protein Vegan Blueberry Maple Smoothie (Pre-Workout or Meal Replacement)
description: Boost your energy with this high-protein vegan blueberry maple smoothie! Quick to make, packed with antioxidants, and perfect as a pre-workout fuel or breakfast...

items: 200 mL oat milk
30-50g vegan vanilla yogurt
3 tbsp maple syrup
60g of plant protein powder (PBFit, Pea Protein, etc. optional, for added protein)
1 handful of spinach
1 cup frozen blueberries (No ice needed as frozen blueberries chill the smoothie without watering it down.)
Add all of the above ingredients into a 1L blender cup (we used the ninja one). (Adding the liquids first like oat milk, syrup, and yogurt will give you a smoother blend)
Add cool water into the same cup to fill in the gaps. Fill just until it reaches the blueberries at the top.
Blend until smooth and serve!

title: Best Vegan S'Mores Cookies with Flax Egg (Chewy Centers & Easy Prep)
description: The best vegan s'mores cookies! Chewy centers, melted chocolate, and toasted marshmallows. This crowd-pleaser recipe uses a flax egg and is air fryer friendly.

items: 1 cup room temperature vegan butter
1 cup granulated sugar
2 flax egg (2 tbsp ground flax mixed with 6 tbsp water; let sit for 5-10 minutes)
4 tsp vanilla extract
3 cups all-purpose flour (360g)
1/2 teaspoon baking powder
1/2 teaspoon baking soda
1/2 teaspoon salt
10 large vegan marshmallows, cut into smaller pieces
2/3 cup vegan dark chocolate chips
40g sourdough discard (optional)
Create the flax egg by combining 2 tbsp ground flax mixed with 6 tbsp water, give it a brief stir with a fork, and let that sit for 5-10 minutes.
Add the room temperature vegan butter and white sugar to a mixing bowl (ideally stand mixer)
Use stand/handheld electric mixer to cream the butter and sugar together until fluffy (~1 minute).
Add in the flax egg and vanilla to the creamed mixture and mix together briefly.
Add all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt to the creamed butter and sugar mixture and mix together until a thick cookie dough forms.

View the tips section if you’d like to try the air fryer method. Otherwise, preheat the oven to 350F. (Optionally line a pan with parchment paper or use “DaTerra Cucina - Nonstick Ceramic Coated Baking Sheet” as that pan never sticks)
Add chocolate chunks and marshmallow pieces to the cookie dough and gently fold in with a spatula to evenly distribute throughout the dough.
Cover the dough and chill in the freezer for ~10-15 min or until the oven is preheated. (You can skip this step if you’re low on time, it just might be slightly harder to form the cookies into balls)

Roll out balls of 12 evenly sized cookies and place on the baking sheet at least 2 inches apart from each other. No need to flatten them as they will spread while baking. Roll out another 12 evenly sized cookies.
Bake for 16-18 minutes until bottoms are lightly browned and the cookies are cooked through but have slightly soft centers.
Remove the cookie tray from the oven and immediately tap the tray on the counter for a more “wrinkly” cookie and help deflate the cookies.
Let the cookies cool on the baking sheet for 5-10 minutes.
Serve!

tips: Be sure to use this baking sheet if you can: “DaTerra Cucina - Nonstick Ceramic Coated Baking Sheet” since nothing sticks to that pan! Otherwise, I’d suggest using some parchment paper in case!
Air Fryer Cookie Cooking Method (makes the cookies look even more like a toasty s’more)
Grease the air fryer basket.
Preheat the air fryer on 400F.
Once preheated fully, add cookies and cook for 8 min.
You’ll need a metal spatula to extract the cookies from the air fryer basket.

title: Easy Creamy Vegan Potato and Leek Soup (Made with Cashews, No Dairy)
description: The easiest creamy vegan potato and leek soup! Rich, cozy, and dairy-free thanks to cashews. Made with minimal ingredients and perfect for a chilly night in.

items: 1 large leek
4-5 russet potatoes
2 cups of cooked white rice (leftover rice is fine)
water (enough to fill the pot)
vegetable broth (Better Than Bullion's no-chicken stock)
3/4 cup raw cashews (salted is fine)
2 tbsp olive oil (to sauté veggies)
2 tbsp miso paste
2-4 tbsp soy sauce
3-4 tbsp lemon juice
Dill to top the soup (optional)

steps.name: Prep the vegetables
items: Clean and cut the leek into ½ inch pieces. When you get to the leaves, make sure that you clean the inner layers, piece by piece to remove sand or dirt.
Chop russet potatoes into 1-inch cubes.

steps.name: Sauté the leeks
items: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium/high heat. Add leeks with a pinch of salt and sauté until soft and lightly charred.

steps.name: Build the soup base
items: Add the chopped potatoes and cashews to the pot.
Pour in boiling water to cover the vegetables by about half an inch.
Add vegan bullion and stir to combine.

steps.name: Simmer and season
items: Simmer uncovered on medium/low for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Add 2 cups of leftover rice and immersion blend to desired texture.
Season to taste with salt, pepper.

steps.name: Finish the soup
items: Turn off the heat.
Stir in soy sauce, miso, and lemon juice.
Top with dill or additional herbs before serving.

tips: Using leftover rice adds creaminess and body to the soup without dairy.

title: Easy Vegan Gazpacho (Classic Spanish-Style, No-Cook Summer Soup)
description: Yes, traditional Spanish gazpacho is naturally vegan. This easy no-cook summer soup blends ripe tomatoes, cucumber, basil, and olive oil into a fresh, refreshin...

items: 1 ¾ lb (or 800g) of fresh tomatoes
1 medium cucumber
1 bell pepper
1 clove of garlic
½ onion
1 slice of stale bread
1 cup loosely packed (or 30g) fresh basil
4 tbsp of olive oil
2 tbsp sherry vinegar
salt to taste
ground black pepper to taste
toast (for dipping into the soup, optional)

Roughly chop the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, and onion. You don’t need to chop it too finely as all but the reserved garnish will be blended (set aside a small amount of the chopped veggie mix to garnish the soup).
Mince the garlic clove.
Tear up 3/4 of your basil leaves.
Chop up the stale bread into smaller pieces.
Add the veggies, garlic, basil leaves, and stale bread into a large mixing bowl (except for the reserved garnish).
Drizzle a decent amount of extra virgin olive oil and vinegar on top of the chopped mix in the large mixing bowl.
Season well with salt and ground black pepper.
Put the mixing bowl covered in the fridge for 30 mins to chill and let the vinegar and spice mix infuse with the veggies to boost the soup’s flavor.
Pour the mixing bowl mixture into a blender, and then blend until smooth and creamy.
Taste the soup and adjust seasoning as you see fit. (Like some fancy, thin, flaky sea salt)
To serve, ladle the gazpacho into bowls, and then top it with a spoonful of the reserved chopped vegetables, fresh basil leaves, and a splash of olive oil.
It’s very tasty alongside vegan sourdough focaccia. Enjoy!

title: Quick Vegan Air Fryer Calzones with Premade Pizza Dough (No Oven Needed)
description: Make a quick dinner with this vegan air fryer calzone recipe! Uses premade dough and cooks in 8 minutes flat with no oven needed. Features a flavorful smoked pa...

items: 1 vegan pizza dough (you can get premade vegan pizza dough at Walmart)
¼ cup of all-purpose flour
2 tbsp of olive oil (one for inner part of the calzone, one for outer crust)
2 vegan sausages (frozen)
salt to taste
oregano to taste
garlic to taste (minced)
handful of spinach
½ vegan shredded mozzarella
tomato paste (I prefer tubed)
dash of smoked paprika (for the outer part of the calzone)
dash of ground turmeric (for the outer part of the calzone)
dash of garlic powder (for the outer part of the calzone)

Throw in the vegan sausage into the air fryer and cook to package instructions. At the halfway point, you can speed up the cook time by cutting it in half. It’s also good to cook the sausage first, so that it preheats the air fryer for the calzones themselves!

While the sausage is cooking, grab two baking sheets and throw all purpose flour on each pan so that when you flatten the dough to make the 2 calzones on each pan, it doesn’t stick to the pans. The baking sheets are mainly just to keep the area clean, making sure flour and oil doesn’t get everywhere, making for a speedy clean up at the end!
Remove the vegan pizza dough from the packaging and divide the pizza dough into 4 equal pieces.

Flatten each piece into a longer oval onto the baking sheet, coating each side with a little bit of flour. Try to flatten the dough as thin as you can get it without tearing (~1-2mm and slightly translucent when you hold the dough up in the light).
Once you’re done flattening the dough, add a little bit more flour beneath it, just so if it warms up as you add toppings, that it doesn’t stick to the pan or tear.
With a spoon, drop on a spoonful or two of olive oil and spread it all over the dough up to the edges. You can use the spoon to flatten the dough more too if you see it’s bunching up again.
Add salt and oregano to the olive oil-covered dough (the salt is there since the tomato paste isn’t salted)
Add pre-chopped garlic to the dough and spread thin (you can also use garlic powder if you don’t have prepped garlic)
Add tomato paste (or 2-3 spoonfuls of crushed tomato puree) and spread thin.
Add vegan cheese and top it with some spinach leaves.
Once the vegan sausage is done, take it out of the air fryer and chop it into small pieces, add the pieces also on top of the calzone.
Add more vegan cheese to keep your toppings in check.
You can also add anything else to the calzone, but I would recommend keeping the water-content low if you can.

Fold over the oval such that it looks like an empanada, then close it by pinching the sides. You can prevent spilling by folding the edges over and crimp / roll them to create a decorative, braided seal. Ideally keep the seal up, so no juices leak into the air fryer.
Spoon a little bit of olive oil on each calzone top, then sprinkle on tumeric, smoked paprika, and garlic powder (this adds some pizazz).

Pop the calzones into the pre-heated (from the sausage) air fryer on 400F and cook for a total of 8 min. Flip the calzones halfway to slightly more than halfway of the cook time so that both sides cook evenly. It is essential that you flip halfway! Do not flip if they aren’t fully crunchy on the top half, or it could break. If they are sticking together, don’t worry, just flip them and they should unstick as the flipped side cooks. Flipping ensures that  bottom gets cooked through enough and not be soft or still wet.
You’ll know the calzones are done when the crust on both sides is crispy and slightly golden brown.
Repeat once more for the other 2 calzones.

title: 5-Minute Vegan Microwave Fudge Squares (No-Bake, Oat Milk Chocolate)
description: These 5-minute vegan fudge squares use oat milk and dark chocolate, melted in the microwave and chilled until fudgy for a fast, no-bake vegan dessert.

items: ¾ cup oat milk (unsweetened and unflavored)
1 ½ cup vegan dark chocolate chips
cocoa powder (optional)
crushed peppermint candy (optional)

steps.name: Melt the chocolate
items: Grab a small, rectangular microwave-safe glass container.
Add the oat milk and dark chocolate to the container.
Microwave in 30-second intervals, stirring after each round, until the chocolate is fully melted and smooth.

steps.name: Chill the fudge
items: Cover the container and place it in the freezer for about 2 hours, or until fully set.

steps.name: Slice and serve
items: Sprinkle with cocoa powder, flaky sea salt, crushed peppermint, or chopped nuts if desired.
Cut the fudge into squares directly in the container and serve.

tips: If you want a smaller quantity, just have milk to vegan dark chocolate ratio be 1:2
Small dark chocolate chips will melt easier, but if all you have is a bar, you might want to chop that up to quicken the melt time.

title: Creamy Vegan Elote (Grilled Mexican Street Corn with Tajín & Lime)
description: Wow your friends with this creamy, zesty vegan elote! Grilled corn coated in dairy-free sour cream and mayo, then topped with bold Tajín and fresh lime.

items: 2-4 ears of corn
Vegan mayonnaise
Vegan sour cream
tajin seasoning to taste
lime juice to taste
fresh cilantro, chopped
Boil the corn until fully cooked.
While the corn is boiling, mix a sauce using about 60% vegan mayonnaise and 40% vegan sour cream in a small bowl. Make enough to coat all the corn.
Roast the corn on the grill until slightly charred.
Once slightly cooled, spread a thin layer of the creamy sauce over each ear of corn.
Sprinkle with Tajín, a squeeze of lime juice, and chopped cilantro before serving.

title: Quick Vegan Thai Red Curry with Air Fryer Tofu (Maesri Paste)
description: Craving Thai food? This quick vegan red curry uses Maesri paste and crispy air fryer tofu to make a flavorful, restaurant-style meal in under 30 minutes.

items: 1 (4 oz) can Thai Red Curry Paste (Maesri)
1 can full-fat coconut milk
1–2 tbsp coconut oil
1 block firm tofu
1 red onion, sliced
1 red bell pepper, sliced
1 cup spinach
2–3 tbsp soy sauce
2 tbsp rice wine vinegar, to taste (optional)
2 tbsp lime juice (optional)
1–2 tbsp sesame oil, to taste (optional)
1 C jasmine rice (cooked)

steps.name: Prepare the rice and tofu
items: Begin cooking the rice according to package directions.

Cut the tofu into small cubes and air fry at 400°F for 15–20 minutes, shaking halfway through, until lightly crispy. If you don’t have an air fryer, press the tofu and shallow fry it in a pan while prepping the curry.

steps.name: Build the curry base
items: Heat 1–2 tablespoons of coconut oil in a deep pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Chop the red onion and bell pepper into bite-sized pieces, then sauté until lightly charred but still crisp (or to your preference).
Stir in the coconut milk, Thai red curry paste, and rice wine vinegar (if using) until well combined.

steps.name: Finish and serve
items: Add the cooked tofu, spinach, soy sauce, sesame oil, and lime juice.
Stir gently, then remove from heat to preserve the bright flavors.
Serve hot over freshly cooked rice.

tips: Feel free to use vegan chick strips instead of tofu or substitute in any different veggies, curry paste bases! Maesri has a tasty variety pack to mix things up.

title: Air Fryer Tofu Stir Fry: Quick Vegan Weeknight Dinner
description: Fast, flavorful, healthy weeknight dinner! This air fryer tofu stir fry is a quick vegan meal with crispy tofu, garlic, spinach, and simple pantry ingredients.

items: 1 tbsp olive oil (or preferred cooking oil)
1 block firm tofu
1 clove of garlic, minced
3 cups spinach
red pepper flakes to taste
1 tsp minced ginger (optional)
1 tsp sesame oil (optional)
2 tbsp rice wine vinegar (optional)
Soy sauce, to taste
2 tbsp sesame seeds
1 C cooked white rice

steps.name: Cook the rice
items: Start cooking the rice in a medium saucepan.

steps.name: Crisp the tofu
items: While the rice cooks, cut the tofu into small cubes and air fry at 400°F for about 15 minutes, turning halfway through.

steps.name: Sauté aromatics and combine
items: When the tofu has about 3 minutes left, heat 1 tbsp of oil in a skillet. Add garlic, ginger, and red chili flakes, and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the tofu, soy sauce, sesame oil, and rice wine vinegar to the skillet, adjusting to taste.
Stir in the spinach and cook until wilted, about 1 minute.
Taste and adjust seasonings or add more soy sauce as desired.

steps.name: Serve
items: Serve the tofu and spinach mixture over the cooked rice.

tips: You can make this stir fry without an air fryer, but pan-frying tofu will take longer.
Using an air fryer keeps tofu crispy and golden, perfect for quick vegan weeknight dinners.

title: Easy Vegan Lemon Granita (Sweet & Tart No-Churn Italian Ice)
description: Craving Italian ice? Make this easy, sweet & tart vegan lemon granita! A no-churn dessert that requires minimal ingredients. Optional liqueur for a softer, icy ...

items: 3 lemons (preferably organic, for zest)
2 cups water
¼ cup granulated sugar (adjust to taste)
Lime juice, to taste
¼ cup orange liqueur (Grand Marnier, optional)
Wash the lemons thoroughly and use a knife to remove the peel in long, thin strips. Try to avoid the white pith, as it can be bitter.
In a medium saucepan, combine the water and sugar. Heat over medium heat until the sugar dissolves, stirring occasionally. Add the lemon peel strips to the syrup.
Remove the syrup from heat and let the lemon peel steep in the syrup for 15–20 minutes. This will extract the oils and flavor from the peel.
Remove the lemon peel by straining the syrup into a bowl. Press lightly on the peel to extract all the flavor. Let the syrup cool completely.
Pour the cooled syrup into a shallow dish or baking pan. Place it in the freezer.

After 1–2 hours, when the mixture starts to freeze around the edges, use a fork to scrape it into small crystals. Return it to the freezer. Repeat this process every 30–60 minutes until the entire mixture has a fluffy, icy texture (about 3–4 hours).
Serve - Fluff the granita one last time with a fork before serving. Scoop into bowls or glasses and enjoy!

tips: I’d suggest adding a liqueur (orange is nice!) to the lemon ice before freezing to ensure that it’s easier to shave the ice given how it helps lower the freezing point. It helps with texture and adds a subtle boozy note.

title: Easy Crispy Roasted Artichoke Hearts (Sheet Pan Side Dish)
description: The easiest side dish ever! Get crispy roasted artichoke hearts in minutes using canned quarters and a sheet pan. Only 4 ingredients and 10 minutes of prep time...

items: 2 cans of quartered artichoke hearts
salt to taste
ground black pepper to taste
olive oil to taste
Preheat your oven to 425°F.
Drain 2 cans of quartered artichoke hearts. Use paper towels to dry them as much as possible.
Spread the artichoke hearts onto a sheet pan.
Season with a big pinch each of salt and black pepper.
Drizzle with 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil.
Toss to coat, then spread them out on the sheet pan so they don’t touch.
Roast for 15 minutes, then toss the artichokes and rotate the pan.
Roast until crispy and golden brown on both sides, 4 min more.

title: Pillowy Vegan Focaccia (Same-Day or Cold Proof Option)
description: Stop buying overpriced bread! Make perfect vegan focaccia at home. This recipe yields a pillowy inside, crunchy crust, and offers flexible proofing (same-day or...

ingredients.name: Bread (No-Sourdough Option)
items: 4 cups bread flour
2 teaspoons salt
3 teaspoons instant yeast
2 cups water (at different altitudes, you may need to adjust the amount of liquid you add.)

ingredients.name: Bread Toppings
items: Salt (to taste)
Garlic powder (optional - to taste)
Rosemary (optional - to taste)
Red pepper flakes (optional - to taste)
Whisk together the flour, salt, and yeast, then add water.
Use a spatula to stir.
Slick the surface of the dough with olive oil; then cover the bowl with a lid/cloth.
Transfer the dough to a baking sheet. Leave the dough on the pan for 30 min so it puffs up more. Flatten it to the edges of the baking sheet with a spatula.
Dimple the dough so that you get some air bubbles! Add generous salt, garlic powder, rosemary, red pepper flakes.
Transfer to the oven immediately and bake at 450ºF for 25 minutes or until golden all around.
Store the focaccia in an airtight container, or leave on the pan but covered with foil.

tips: Experiment with smoky salt, finely chopped olives, adding a tbsp or 2 of non-dairy milk for extra crispiness (the milk gives the yeast more “food”)

title: Crispy Vegan Agedashi Tofu (Air Fryer & Coconut Oil Fry Method)
description: Recreate restaurant-quality agedashi tofu at home! This vegan recipe uses an air fryer and shallow fry for crispy tofu and features a savory, homemade Kombu das...

ingredients.name: Broth
items: 1 (4-inch) vegan kombu
4 cups water
½ cup soy sauce
½ cup Sushi Chef 10 fl. oz. Mirin (Sweetened Sake) (or another mirin, but you likely will need to add more sweetness through balsamic vinegar / maple syrup - add in 1 tbsp increments to taste)
2 tbsp rice vinegar (or 4 tbsp of balsamic vinegar)
Finely chopped scallion

ingredients.name: Tofu
items: 1 firm tofu block (pressed or pre-pressed)
6 Tbsp cornstarch
2–3 Tbsp coconut oil
Boil 4 cups water.
Add kombu and scallions to a pot with hot water.
Stir in soy sauce, mirin, and rice vinegar (or balsamic).
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Cut tofu into 10 pieces.
Coat each piece in corn starch.
Air-fry 15–17 min (flip halfway)
Then, shallow fry in coconut oil until golden.
Pour broth into bowls.
Top with crispy tofu.

steps.name: Notes / Tips
items: Too bitter? Add balsamic, maple syrup, sugar.
Too sweet? Add vinegar.
Too plain? Add soy sauce.
Scallions are optional but add depth.
You can skip the shallow fry if you really want, but it won’t get as crispy of an outer texture! (I haven’t tried it either)

title: High-Protein Vegan Tahini Date Balls (No-Bake, 4-Ingredient Energy Bites)
description: These vegan tahini date balls are a quick, no-bake energy snack made with just 4 simple ingredients. Naturally sweetened with dates and packed with healthy fats...

items: 1 cup Medjool dates, pitted
1 cup walnuts
⅓ cup tahini
Sesame seeds, for rolling (optional but recommended)
In a food processor fitted with an S-blade, blend all ingredients except the sesame seeds until a sticky mixture forms.
Roll the mixture into bite-sized balls and place them on a lined baking sheet (or directly into a container if not coating).
Roll the balls in sesame seeds on the backing sheet to coat, if desired.
Enjoy immediately, or refrigerate for a quick and energizing snack later.

title: Vegan & Gluten-Free Carrot Cake Balls (Oat Flour, Maple Sweetened)
description: Delicious, spiced, and healthy! These vegan and gluten-free carrot cake balls are made with oat flour and maple syrup. Great for meal prep and freezing for late...

items: ¼ cup softened vegan butter
¼ teaspoon vanilla extract
1½ cups powdered sugar
2 tablespoons plant-based milk
Add softened vegan butter to a large mixing bowl and beat with an electric hand mixer until light and fluffy, about 1 minute.
Mix in the vanilla extract until combined.
Gradually add powdered sugar, about ½ cup at a time, mixing until smooth and fluffy.
Add dairy-free milk 1 tablespoon at a time until the desired consistency is reached.
Use immediately, or store the frosting in the refrigerator for up to 1 week or in the freezer for up to 1 month.

tips: Don’t underbake the balls - Make sure that they’re beginning to brown around the edges before you remove them from the oven so they don’t break apart
Leave the balls on the baking sheet for at least 5 minutes before transferring them to a rack so they can harden and keep their shape
Freeze the extras - they last longer and you can pop one in the fridge for the day you’d like to eat it

title: Quick Vegan Peanut Butter Ramen (Savory Sauce with Gochujang & Lime)
description: Craving comfort food? Make this quick vegan peanut butter ramen in under 15 minutes! Toss noodles in a savory Gochujang and lime sauce for a perfect weeknight m...

items: 3 tbsp peanut butter
2 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari)
1 ½ tbsp sriracha (or gochujang)
1 ½ tbsp sesame oil
1 tbsp lime juice
2 packs (3 oz each) vegan ramen noodles (no seasoning packets)
2 tbsp thinly sliced scallions (optional)
Bring a medium saucepan of water to a boil over medium-high heat.
In a bowl, whisk together peanut butter, soy sauce, gochujang, sesame oil, and lime juice.
Cook the ramen noodles for about 3 minutes, then drain, reserving 1 cup of the cooking water.
Whisk ½ cup of the reserved hot water into the peanut butter sauce.
Toss the noodles with the peanut butter sauce, adding additional water 1 tablespoon at a time until the desired consistency is reached.
Top with scallions, if using, and serve.

title: Quick Vegan Bagel Burger (20-Minute Beyond Patty & Cream Cheese)
description: This vegan bagel burger is a quick 20-minute weeknight meal made with an air-fried Beyond Burger, everything bagel, and creamy vegan cheese.

items: 1 vegan burger patty (Beyond Burger or other plant-based patty)
1 vegan everything bagel
3 tbsp vegan cream cheese
4 crinkle cut dill pickles
whole grain mustard to taste
ketchup to taste
hot sauce to taste

steps.name: Air fry the burger patty
items: Cook the Beyond Burger in the air fryer according to package directions, flipping halfway through.

steps.name: Toast and prep the bagel
items: Toast the everything bagel about 5 minutes before the patty finishes cooking.
Spread vegan cream cheese on each half and add pickles to one side.

steps.name: Assemble the bagel burger
items: Place the cooked patty on the bagel, top with mustard and ketchup.
Assemble, slice in half, and drizzle with hot sauce if desired.

tips: We typically cut the bagel in half since it’s easier to pick up any everything bagel seasoning that may fall off.
Quality bagels work best since it’s one of the main ingredients.
You can double the recipe with the same cook time in the air fryer.
Cooking the burger in the air fryer keeps it juicy inside while cutting down on oil and cleanup.

title: Traditional-Style Vegan Baklava with Maple Glaze (Layered Nut & Phyllo Dessert)
description: Yes, vegan baklava can be crispy and delicious. This easy layered nut and phyllo dessert uses a maple syrup glaze for a naturally vegan treat that sets perfectl...

items: 1 lb vegan phyllo dough (16 oz)
1 lb chopped mixed nuts (walnuts, pistachios, almonds, or dried fruit)
1 tsp ground cinnamon
1 cup vegan butter
1 cup granulated sugar
1 cup water
½ cup maple syrup (or agave nectar)
1 tsp vanilla extract

steps.name: Prepare the baklava layers
items: Confirm phyllo dough is fully thawed before starting.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Mix chopped nuts or dried fruit with cinnamon and set aside.
Brush a 9×13-inch pan with vegan butter. (I always use this nonstick sheet (not sponsored I just love it), and nothing ever sticks on that pan, not even vegan marshmallows!).
Layer two sheets of phyllo in the baking pan and brush the sheets up to the edges with the slightly melted vegan butter.
Repeat three more times so you have 8 sheets total before the chopped nut or fruit layer.
Sprinkle the chopped nut (and maybe dried fruit) mixture all over the phyllo sheet.
Now, repeat what we did earlier where we add two sheets of dough, then brush the sheet with butter and repeat the process until the remaining 6 sheets are left.
Using a sharp knife, score the top into diamond shapes so that the tasty sugar syrup topping can soak into the edges later!

steps.name: Bake the baklava
items: Bake the baklava for ~45 minutes, until golden brown on top. While baking, you can move onto the next section where we will make the sugar syrup topping to top the baklava once it’s done cooking!

steps.name: Make the syrup
items: While the baklava bakes, boil sugar and water in a small saucepan.
Remove from heat, add maple syrup, then simmer on low for 20 minutes.

steps.name: Assemble and add syrup
items: Pour syrup evenly over hot baklava.
Allow to cool fully so the syrup absorbs properly.

tips: Feel free to half the recipe if you are short on time or don’t feel like having as much in such a short time if you’re making it just for yourself! The baklava will only take up half a baking sheet, and will only take half the time to make since assembling the sheets is the longest step of the process in my opinion!
For best results, pour the syrup over hot baklava so it absorbs evenly without making the layers soggy.

title: Creamy Vegan Cauliflower Pesto Soup (Dairy-Free, Fall Comfort Meal)
description: The ultimate fall comfort food! This creamy, herby vegan cauliflower pesto soup is entirely dairy-free. Easy to make and perfect topped with crunchy pine nuts a...

items: 1 tbsp olive oil
4 cloves of minced garlic
1 head (~1 lb) cauliflower
4 cups vegetable broth
½ tsp salt
ground black pepper
1 tbsp cornstarch
2 tbsp pine nuts (or sesame seeds!)
1 C loosely packed fresh basil
Red pepper flakes (optional)

Trim the cauliflower, removing the leaves and core and chop it into even ~ 1 in pieces. You don’t need to cut the cauliflower too much as we will immersion blend it later to create a creamy soup. Then set the pieces of cauliflower aside for later.
Next, mince 4 garlic cloves.

Then, heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a large pot over low-medium heat and immediately add the minced garlic to the pot, starting a gentle fry. Let the garlic slowly sizzle as the oil heats up. Cooking the garlic this way will lead to crispy garlic from the slow evaporation of water in the garlic as well as provide a controlled Maillard reaction which will give you a more nutty flavor without creating bitterness! Cook the garlic for 1 minute, until lightly golden brown.

Once the garlic is ready, add the chopped cauliflower pieces, 3 cups of vegetable broth, and then salt and pepper to taste. Bring the soup to a boil, then cover the pot and let the broth simmer 10–12 minutes, until the cauliflower pieces are tender.
In a small bowl, whisk the remaining 1 cup of vegetable broth with cornstarch until smooth.
Stir the cornstarch mixture into the larger pot of soup and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.

Optional step - If you’d like to top your soup with toasty nuts, while the soup is simmering for 5 minutes, do the following: In a small, dry skillet over low heat, toast the pine nuts (or sesame seeds) until fragrant and golden.
Lastly, add all but a few basil leaves to the large pot of soup, and then remove it from heat.
Use an immersion blender to puree the soup until smooth and creamy, or leave in a few chunks of cauliflower in it if you’d prefer.
Taste the soup, and adjust seasoning as needed like adding additional salt and pepper, or topping the soup with some red pepper flakes for a bit of a kick.
Ladle the soup into bowls, and top them with remaining basil, a drizzle of olive oil, and toasted pine nuts (or sesame seeds).

tips: Try pickling a few cauliflower florets or adding finely diced carrots for a little crunch and color. No cooking needed, just cut the pieces very small so they don’t overpower the soup!

title: Creamy Vegan Saffron Risotto (Milanese Style with Vegan Butter & Turmeric)
description: Master creamy, classic vegan risotto! This Milanese-style recipe uses Arborio rice and vegan butter for richness. Optional saffron and savory garlic-fried mushr...

items: 2 tbsp olive oil
1 small yellow onion, diced (or white onion)
1 ½ cups arborio rice
3 cups vegetable broth
2 tbsp white wine (or white wine vinegar)
4 tbsp vegan butter
1 tsp ground turmeric (or finely ground saffron, if available)
2 tsp salt
ground black pepper to taste

ingredients.name: Optional Bonus Ingredients
items: 2 tbsp olive oil
2 cloves of minced garlic
½–¾ lb portobello mushrooms, sliced
salt to taste
ground black pepper to taste
lemon juice to taste
dried parsley to taste (or fresh or frozen)
Bring the vegetable broth to a gentle boil, then lower to a simmer.
In a deep nonstick saucepan, heat olive oil over medium heat.
Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent.
Stir in the arborio rice and toast for 1–2 minutes.
Add white wine (or vinegar) and stir until mostly absorbed.
Gradually add the broth, about ½ cup at a time, stirring often. Wait until most of the liquid is absorbed before adding more.
When about 1 cup of broth remains, stir in the peas.
Add the final cup of broth and cook until the rice is creamy and tender.
Reduce heat to medium-low, then stir in vegan butter until melted and smooth.
Add turmeric or saffron, salt, and pepper. Adjust seasoning to taste.

tips: Use short-grain rice like arborio or carnaroli for proper creaminess.
Saffron gives authentic flavor and color; turmeric is a good substitute for color only.
Add broth gradually as pouring the liquid all in at once prevents the risotto from developing its signature texture.

title: Easy Tahini Halva (3 Ingredients, Naturally Vegan)
description: Yes, traditional tahini halva is naturally vegan. This easy 3-ingredient version uses maple syrup for a simpler, no-thermometer recipe inspired by Middle Easter...

items: ¾ cups maple syrup
1 and ½ cups tahini (like Lebanon Valley Tahini Sesame Paste)
3 tsp vanilla extract

steps.name: Boil the Maple Syrup
items: Place the maple syrup in a medium saucepan and heat over medium heat until it reaches 266°F (130°C). The syrup will bubble and foam, which is normal. Do not move the pot or turn off the heat until it reaches temperature or develops a slightly roasted aroma, which signals proper crystallization for good texture. If it smells like it’s burning, remove it from the heat. This can happen if the saucepan is too wide and the syrup is too shallow to get an accurate reading.

steps.name: Mix in the Tahini
items: Once the maple syrup has properly crystallized, remove it from the heat and immediately stir in the tahini and vanilla extract until the mixture thickens and loses its shiny appearance. Stir as quickly as possible, as waiting too long can cause the mixture to clump. Continue stirring until smooth and velvety.
Pour the mixture immediately into a 6 x 9 inch glass container, or two smaller single-portion containers, and spread it into an even layer with a spatula.
Sprinkle crushed pistachios or other nuts or chopped dried fruit on top, if desired, and gently press them into the surface.

steps.name: Set and Chill
items: Freeze the halva for at least 3 hours so it firms up enough to slice cleanly.
For a softer, fudgier texture, you can refrigerate it for about 24 hours instead, though the freezer is much faster.

tips: Make this before dinner to give it enough time to solidify in the freezer.
Darker maple syrup is easier to boil and handle with this recipe.
Removing the mixture from heat too early will give a softer, fudgier texture.
If tahini and vanilla aren’t added immediately, the mixture may look clumpy or oily. You can pour off excess oil to salvage it and it will still taste great.
Cooking too long, or using sugar instead of maple syrup, can make it slightly grainy with a more roasted flavor, but it’s still delicious.
